subject.title: perf(dev): gateway:watch triggers full rebuild on every startup when working tree is dirty

question: Should dirty watched source trees fall through to mtime freshness when the build stamp is current, or should any dirty watched source continue to force a rebuild?
rationale: Current source proves the reported performance cost, but current tests and the gateway-watch regression helper encode the conservative dirty-tree rebuild as intentional behavior, so automation should not change the contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt mtime freshness for dirty trees
options.body: Dirty watched trees would skip rebuilds when no watched file is newer than the build stamp, with tests and gateway-watch regression logic updated to match.

options.title: Keep conservative dirty rebuilds
options.body: The current behavior stays intentional, and the linked fallthrough PRs should be closed or declined as trading correctness margin for developer-loop speed.

options.title: Design stronger freshness tracking
options.body: Maintain the current rebuild behavior until a hash or stamp strategy can distinguish dirty-but-built files from dirty stale files without relying only on mtimes.

recommendation.title: Adopt mtime freshness for dirty trees
recommendation.body: Dirty watched trees would skip rebuilds when no watched file is newer than the build stamp, with tests and gateway-watch regression logic updated to match.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` introduced the dirty-tree optimization and has recent adjacent ownership in the run-node script surface.
